whatWorks: Seed 5134 is the one token that actually delivers the brief: a bone body with verdigris tendrils budding outward at uneven intervals, and its market states are legible at 120px because the tendrils visibly retract inward under stress and extend past the body under recovery. This seed is the proof the runtime can do COLONY, and it must not be normalised away when the other eleven are fixed.

The identity anchors hold with real discipline: every one of the twelve sits on the same deep ink ground, uses only verdigris and bone, and is centred and radial. There is no stray hue, no off-centre composition and no drifting ground across seeds or states, so the collection already reads as one body of work.

The outer boundary of the denser seeds (5396, 5920, 6051) is genuinely ragged rather than a clean circle, because overlapping members break the silhouette at varied radius. That jaggedness is the only place accretion is currently visible, and it is doing the work the brief asks of rhythm.

findings.whatFails: Ten of the twelve seeds are annuli with a large empty ink hole punched through the exact centre (5003, 5658, 5396, 5265, 5789, 5920, 6051, 6313 most severely), and the 512px single is a thin ring of scattered squares around a void that occupies roughly a third of the composition.
findings.why: The direction states that one dense centre dominates and members thin outward so the eye starts at the core. The rendered work is the precise inverse: the densest ring of matter sits at mid radius and the centre is the emptiest region, so the eye starts at a hole. A colony budding from a shared centre cannot have no centre, and the negativeSpace rule places clear space beyond the colony's reach, not inside it.
findings.specificChange: Remove the inner radius cutoff entirely and place members from radius zero outward, then decrease member count per ring as radius grows so density falls monotonically from the core to the rim. The centre cell should be the largest and most opaque member in the composition, with each successive generation smaller and more sparsely spaced outward.
findings.keep: Keep the radial generational construction and the uneven angular placement that already breaks the outer silhouette, and keep the overall reach of the colony where it currently sits on the dense seeds so the fix fills the hole rather than shrinking the work.

findings.whatFails: The members are hard-edged rectangles and polygons, not rounded forms. Seed 5396 is built from rotated squares with visible corners, 5789 from teal rectangles arranged like cogs, the entire 512px single is a field of small squares, and 6182 is a single hard octagon with straight sides and sharp vertices.
findings.why: Both the medium and the motif translation name rounded primitives as the whole material of the piece, and the brief asks for a biological feeling that is explicitly not geometric. Corners and axis-aligned edges read as tiling, masonry or machinery; the sheet currently reads as gears and mosaic, which is design rather than accretion.
findings.specificChange: Replace the rectangle primitive with circles or ellipses for every member, and where a facetted form is needed increase the corner rounding until no straight edge segment is visible at 120px. Cap eccentricity on the ellipses so members stay near-circular rather than becoming lozenges.
findings.keep: Keep the overlapping and alpha-stacking of members, which is what currently gives the clusters their depth and the mottled interior, and keep the size variation between members that already exists in 5396.

findings.whatFails: On the 120px sheet all twelve are circles of near-identical diameter. Spread is bimodal rather than varied: 5265 and 6313 are small, the remaining ten all reach the same radius. Worse, 6182 renders as a flat featureless teal octagon and 6444 as a flat featureless cream disc with a single dot, so two of twelve carry no colony, no members and no density gradient at all.
findings.why: The variation strategy says tokens differ FIRST in how far the colony has spread and second in how densely it packs, but almost all of the seed-to-seed difference currently lives in interior detail and colour, and interior detail is exactly what the thumbnail intent concedes will not resolve at 120px. What survives is silhouette, and the silhouettes are the same. Two blank plates additionally read as render failures rather than as tokens.
findings.specificChange: Widen the spread parameter to a continuous range spanning roughly a third of the frame to near the frame margin, and spread the seeds evenly across it so the middle spreads that are currently missing get populated. Separately, raise the minimum member count so no seed can render fewer members than are needed to show a density gradient, which removes the 6182 and 6444 blank cases.
findings.keep: Keep the two small-reach seeds 5265 and 6313 as the sparse end of the range, and keep the palette rotation between bone-dominant and verdigris-dominant tokens, which is currently the second most useful separator on the sheet.

findings.whatFails: Across the state rows the colony's reach barely moves. Seed 5003 has an identical inner and outer radius in all three states and changes only by gaining a few small dark crescents. Seed 5265 is nearly indistinguishable across all three rows at any size. Seed 5396 moves in the wrong apparent direction: its stress frame has a much smaller central hole and reads as heavier and more saturated than its neutral and recovery frames.
findings.why: Growth and retreat are stated as the whole market story and the change is required to be plainly visible at thumbnail size. Three of the four sampled seeds fail that, and 5396 fails it in the most damaging way, because pulling members inward while holding the outer radius fixed closes the void and increases apparent mass, so stress reads as more colony rather than less.
findings.specificChange: Bind the colony's outer radius directly to market state so stress contracts overall reach by a clearly visible fraction and recovery extends it beyond neutral, and decrease total member count under stress at the same time so mass falls with reach instead of concentrating. Contract the outer rim inward rather than migrating members toward the centre.
findings.keep: Keep the seed 5134 behaviour, where tendrils retract under stress and extend under recovery, and keep every token recognisably the same token across its three states, which the current sheet does achieve.

findings.whatFails: The palette splits into two extremes with nothing in between. Seeds 5003, 5658, 6444 and 5527 are large masses of near-white bone on near-black ink, which is the highest contrast pairing available. At the other end 5265 and the 512px single render at such low luminance that the members are barely separable from the ground and the piece nearly disappears.
findings.why: The palette intent specifies damp and mineral verdigris and bone over deep ink at LOW contrast, so the forms read as biological rather than bright. Blown-out bone on ink reads as high-key graphic poster work, and the near-black seeds read as an underexposed render rather than as a deliberate quiet token. Neither end is damp.
findings.specificChange: Darken the bone toward a greyed, slightly green-shifted off-white and lift the ink ground a step toward a desaturated blue-black, narrowing the luminance range between the brightest member and the ground. At the dark end, raise the minimum member luminance so the faintest seed still separates clearly from the ground at 120px.
findings.keep: Keep the verdigris and bone pairing itself and the deep ink ground as the only three colour families, and keep the alpha overlap that produces intermediate tones where members stack, which is currently the most mineral-looking thing in the palette.

overall: The runtime is producing a disciplined, coherent radial system with a consistent ink ground and a clean verdigris and bone palette, and seed 5134 shows it can genuinely render COLONY as briefed. But the collection as rendered is not the thing the brief asked for: it is a set of rings, gears and rosettes rather than a growth budding from a shared centre. The single most damaging fault is that the centre is a hole in ten of twelve seeds, which inverts the stated focal hierarchy and puts negative space inside the colony instead of beyond it. Compounding that, the members are hard-edged squares and polygons rather than rounded primitives, so the work reads mechanical rather than biological, and the even angular spacing on 5789, 5920 and 6051 makes several tokens read as turbines. At 120px, the size the collection is actually browsed at, the twelve seeds collapse into one circular silhouette of near-identical diameter with all the variation hiding in interior detail that does not survive the downscale, and two of the twelve render as flat featureless plates. Finally, the market story is not being told: three of four sampled seeds barely move between states and 5396 appears to gain mass under stress. Fill the centre, round the primitives, and drive both seed variation and market state through the colony's outer reach rather than through its interior, and the rest of the system is already in place to support it.
